clusters.title: [Impact] KB5099414 on Config1 - Shell spoofing vs WinExe manifest identity
clusters.body:
<!-- impact:shell-launch:Config1 -->

Impact analysis conducted on source code version:

- https://github.com/defrances/HostApplication - commit `22b249a754b849dac151e976b533f60994fc6098`

## Updates applicable for this product configuration

| Title | Package | CVEs | Recommendation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Windows Shell Spoofing Vulnerability | [KB5099414](https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/vulnerability/CVE-2026-32202) | CVE-2026-32202 | Low Prio |

## Product Configuration Specification

- Product configuration: `Config1`
- Model / role: `CTConsole-A300` / `ct-imaging-workstation`
- Deployment group: `imaging-ct`
- OS: `Windows 11 IoT Enterprise` build `10.0.22621.2500`
- Clinical criticality: `high`
- Network exposure: `restricted_lan`

## Vendor vs product scores

| | Severity | Likelihood | Risk |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Vendor | `C` | `C` | `C` |
| Product | `L` | `L` | `L` |

## Technical Impact Assessment

### Impacted Components

`HostApplication.csproj` `OutputType=WinExe` and `app.manifest` `assemblyIdentity` define how Windows launches the product executable.

### Potential Risks

- **Required for the app to keep working: Not required.** Executable identity is declared in `app.manifest`; Shell components are not PackageReferences.
- **If we install: App may break.** Shell cumulative updates can change Explorer presentation of WinExe identities until reboot.
- **If we skip: No effect on the app.** FindUpdates BLOCK/HOLD: skipping does not block Host Application startup; bundled runtime is unchanged.
- **Compatibility: Compatible with the app.** WinExe on `main` already starts on this image; policy keeps the row at Low Prio.

### Conclusions

Shell KB does not alter bits inside the published self-contained executable.

## Cybersecurity impact assessment

This patch fixes CVE-2026-32202 in Windows Shell. SBOM scan and source code scan revealed there is no such dependency in our code. No shell32 usage in `MainViewModel` or Core libraries on `main`.

## Product Risk assessment

- **Functions affected:** Launch via WinExe/manifest only; notes, sysinfo, and bulletin paths unchanged if KB is skipped.
- **Hazards:** None identified for this product configuration when the update is not installed.
- **Install vs skip:** Install still carries shell servicing risk; skip aligns with FindUpdates BLOCK and does not stop the app.

## Test Planning

### Recommended Regression Suite

- None. No documented test covers this coupling.

### Gap Analysis

- None. No documented test covers shell-launch coupling.

## Recommendation

Maintain FindUpdates BLOCK on this configuration: record Low Prio evidence only; do not treat as product patch authorization.

clusters.title: [Impact] dwm-wpf on Config2 - DWM stack touches PerMonitorV2 WPF chrome
clusters.body:
<!-- impact:dwm-wpf:Config2 -->

Impact analysis conducted on source code version:

- https://github.com/defrances/HostApplication - commit `22b249a754b849dac151e976b533f60994fc6098`

## Updates applicable for this product configuration

| Title | Package | CVEs | Recommendation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Microsoft DWM Core Library Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability | [KB5093998](https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/vulnerability/CVE-2026-45637) | CVE-2026-45637 | Install - High Prio |
| Desktop Window Manager Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability | [KB5099535](https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/vulnerability/CVE-2026-50692) | CVE-2026-50692 | Install - High Prio |

## Product Configuration Specification

- Product configuration: `Config2`
- Model / role: `LabBench-L110` / `lab-analysis-workstation`
- Deployment group: `lab-ring-0`
- OS: `Windows 11 IoT Enterprise` build `10.0.26100.4200`
- Clinical criticality: `high`
- Network exposure: `restricted_lan`

## Vendor vs product scores

| | Severity | Likelihood | Risk |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Vendor | `H` | `M` | `H` |
| Product | `M` | `L` | `L` |

## Technical Impact Assessment

### Impacted Components

DWM composition for bordered panels in `MainWindow.xaml` with `app.manifest` `PerMonitorV2` DPI awareness.

### Potential Risks

- **Required for the app to keep working: Not required.** Bundled .NET 9 runtime in publish output is unchanged by a DWM KB (no DWM PackageReference).
- **If we install: App may break.** DWM EoP fixes may change compositor behavior around `MainWindow.xaml` chrome after reboot.
- **If we skip: Station stays exposed.** Skipping leaves DWM-class host exposure; HTTPS bulletin and notes flows in Core are unchanged.
- **Compatibility: Compatible with the app.** Current `main` WPF UI runs against today's DWM on the configuration's OS build.

### Conclusions

DWM patches change host compositor behavior, not assemblies inside `HostApplication.exe`.

## Cybersecurity impact assessment

This patch fixes CVE-2026-45637, CVE-2026-50692 in Desktop Window Manager. SBOM scan and source code scan revealed there is no such dependency in our code. WPF relies on host DWM composition; no DWM assembly in the SBOM-backed publish folder.

## Product Risk assessment

- **Functions affected:** WPF UI shell, notes file I/O, and vendor bulletin HTTPS check may indirectly depend on the patched host stack.
- **Hazards:** None identified for bundled-runtime replacement; host exposure persists if the KB is skipped.
- **Install vs skip:** Install may require reboot and targeted smoke; skip leaves host CVE class while self-contained exe still launches.

## Test Planning

### Recommended Regression Suite

- `TC-SMOKE-SYSINFO` — guarded in `docs/test-plan.md`.

### Gap Analysis

- No documented DWM or UI automation tests.

## Recommendation

Proceed with lab validation (Install - High Prio rows above); re-run Smoke and Regression categories from `docs/test-plan.md` after OS servicing and reboot.

clusters.title: [Impact] KB5099444 on Config2 - NoteStore uses host NTFS for AppData I/O
clusters.body:
<!-- impact:ntfs-notes:Config2 -->

Impact analysis conducted on source code version:

- https://github.com/defrances/HostApplication - commit `22b249a754b849dac151e976b533f60994fc6098`

## Updates applicable for this product configuration

| Title | Package | CVEs | Recommendation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Windows NTFS Remote Code Execution Vulnerability | [KB5099444](https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/vulnerability/CVE-2026-50448) | CVE-2026-50448 | Install - High Prio |

## Product Configuration Specification

- Product configuration: `Config2`
- Model / role: `LabBench-L110` / `lab-analysis-workstation`
- Deployment group: `lab-ring-0`
- OS: `Windows 11 IoT Enterprise` build `10.0.26100.4200`
- Clinical criticality: `high`
- Network exposure: `restricted_lan`

## Vendor vs product scores

| | Severity | Likelihood | Risk |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Vendor | `H` | `L` | `L` |
| Product | `M` | `L` | `M` |

## Technical Impact Assessment

### Impacted Components

`NoteStore.cs` persists notes under `%AppData%\HostApplication\notes.txt` using BCL file APIs on the host NTFS volume.

### Potential Risks

- **Required for the app to keep working: Not required.** Notes use `File.ReadAllText` / `File.WriteAllText` only; NTFS filter drivers are not in the solution.
- **If we install: Compatible with the app.** NTFS cumulative updates are usually compatible with AppData file I/O; re-run notes smoke after install.
- **If we skip: Station stays exposed.** Unpatched NTFS leaves the volume backing `%AppData%\HostApplication\notes.txt` exposed while the app still starts.
- **Compatibility: Compatible with the app.** `NoteStoreTests` lock load/save semantics on the host file system today.

### Conclusions

NTFS KBs change the host volume backing AppData, not the self-contained runtime in the zip.

## Cybersecurity impact assessment

This patch fixes CVE-2026-50448 in Windows NTFS. SBOM scan and source code scan revealed there is no such dependency in our code. Product code does not ship an NTFS driver; only consumer file I/O in `NoteStore`.

## Product Risk assessment

- **Functions affected:** WPF UI shell, notes file I/O, and vendor bulletin HTTPS check may indirectly depend on the patched host stack.
- **Hazards:** None identified for bundled-runtime replacement; host exposure persists if the KB is skipped.
- **Install vs skip:** Install may require reboot and targeted smoke; skip leaves host CVE class while self-contained exe still launches.

## Test Planning

### Recommended Regression Suite

- `TC-SMOKE-NOTES` — guarded in `docs/test-plan.md`.
- `TC-UNIT-NOTES-EMPTY` — guarded in `docs/test-plan.md`.
- `TC-UNIT-NOTES-PATH` — guarded in `docs/test-plan.md`.

### Gap Analysis

- None identified.

## Recommendation

Proceed with lab validation (Install - High Prio rows above); re-run Smoke and Regression categories from `docs/test-plan.md` after OS servicing and reboot.

| Windows Win32k Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability | [KB5099536](https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/vulnerability/CVE-2026-54112) | CVE-2026-54112 | Install - High Prio |

## Product Configuration Specification

- Product configuration: `Config2`
- Model / role: `LabBench-L110` / `lab-analysis-workstation`
- Deployment group: `lab-ring-0`
- OS: `Windows 11 IoT Enterprise` build `10.0.26100.4200`
- Clinical criticality: `high`

## Vendor vs product scores

| | Severity | Likelihood | Risk |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Vendor | `H` | `M` | `H` |
| Product | `M` | `L` | `L` |

## Technical Impact Assessment

### Impacted Components

WPF windowing via `MainWindow.xaml`, `UseWPF` in `HostApplication.csproj`, and `app.manifest` (`dpiAware`, `PerMonitorV2`). No Win32k import in source.

### Potential Risks

- **Required for the app to keep working: Not required.** CI publishes `--self-contained true` for `win-x64` (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`); Win32k is not a referenced assembly.
- **If we install: App may break.** Servicing Win32k can shift DPI/window metrics consumed by WPF through `app.manifest` PerMonitorV2 settings.
- **If we skip: Station stays exposed.** Host Win32k flaws remain exploitable on the workstation; `NoteStore` and `InsecureVendorBulletinClient` still run without the KB.
- **Compatibility: Compatible with the app.** Smoke path `TC-SMOKE-SYSINFO` passes on current lab images with existing Win32k behavior.

### Conclusions

Win32k KBs do not replace the self-contained .NET runtime in CI publish output; spot-check WPF layout after servicing.

## Cybersecurity impact assessment

This patch fixes CVE-2026-49805, CVE-2026-50688, CVE-2026-54112, CVE-2026-56176, CVE-2026-57095 in Win32k. SBOM scan and source code scan revealed there is no such dependency in our code. Coupling is indirect through WPF windowing on the host kernel stack.

## Product Risk assessment

- **Functions affected:** WPF UI shell, notes file I/O, and vendor bulletin HTTPS check may indirectly depend on the patched host stack.
- **Hazards:** None identified for bundled-runtime replacement; host exposure persists if the KB is skipped.
- **Install vs skip:** Install may require reboot and targeted smoke; skip leaves host CVE class while self-contained exe still launches.

## Test Planning

### Recommended Regression Suite

- `TC-SMOKE-SYSINFO` — guarded in `docs/test-plan.md`.

### Gap Analysis

- No UI automation or DPI regression case in `docs/test-plan.md`.

## Recommendation

Proceed with lab validation (Install - High Prio rows above); re-run Smoke and Regression categories from `docs/test-plan.md` after OS servicing and reboot.

## Product Configuration Specification

- Product configuration: `Config6`
- Model / role: `PACS-Validate-24H2` / `pacs-review-workstation`
- Deployment group: `pacs-validate`
- OS: `Windows 11 Version 24H2 for x64-based Systems` build `10.0.26100.4200`

- Network exposure: `restricted_lan`

## Vendor vs product scores

| | Severity | Likelihood | Risk |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Vendor | `M` | `M` | `M` |
| Product | `L` | `L` | `L` |

## Technical Impact Assessment

### Impacted Components

WPF windowing via `MainWindow.xaml`, `UseWPF` in `HostApplication.csproj`, and `app.manifest` (`dpiAware`, `PerMonitorV2`). No Win32k import in source.

### Potential Risks

- **Required for the app to keep working: Not required.** CI publishes `--self-contained true` for `win-x64` (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`); Win32k is not a referenced assembly.
- **If we install: App may break.** Servicing Win32k can shift DPI/window metrics consumed by WPF through `app.manifest` PerMonitorV2 settings.
- **If we skip: Station stays exposed.** Host Win32k flaws remain exploitable on the workstation; `NoteStore` and `InsecureVendorBulletinClient` still run without the KB.
- **Compatibility: Compatible with the app.** Smoke path `TC-SMOKE-SYSINFO` passes on current lab images with existing Win32k behavior.

### Conclusions

Win32k KBs do not replace the self-contained .NET runtime in CI publish output; spot-check WPF layout after servicing.

## Cybersecurity impact assessment

This patch fixes CVE-2026-49805, CVE-2026-50688, CVE-2026-54112, CVE-2026-56176, CVE-2026-57095 in Win32k. SBOM scan and source code scan revealed there is no such dependency in our code. Coupling is indirect through WPF windowing on the host kernel stack.

## Product Risk assessment

- **Functions affected:** WPF UI shell, notes file I/O, and vendor bulletin HTTPS check may indirectly depend on the patched host stack.
- **Hazards:** None identified for bundled-runtime replacement; host exposure persists if the KB is skipped.
- **Install vs skip:** Install may require reboot and targeted smoke; skip leaves host CVE class while self-contained exe still launches.

## Test Planning

### Recommended Regression Suite

- `TC-SMOKE-SYSINFO` — guarded in `docs/test-plan.md`.

### Gap Analysis

- No UI automation or DPI regression case in `docs/test-plan.md`.

## Recommendation

Proceed with lab validation (Install - High Prio rows above); re-run Smoke and Regression categories from `docs/test-plan.md` after OS servicing and reboot.

clusters.title: [Impact] KB5099414 on Config7 - Shell spoofing vs WinExe manifest identity
clusters.body:
<!-- impact:shell-launch:Config7 -->

Impact analysis conducted on source code version:

- https://github.com/defrances/HostApplication - commit `22b249a754b849dac151e976b533f60994fc6098`

## Updates applicable for this product configuration

| Title | Package | CVEs | Recommendation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Windows Shell Spoofing Vulnerability | [KB5099414](https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/vulnerability/CVE-2026-32202) | CVE-2026-32202 | Low Prio |

## Product Configuration Specification

- Product configuration: `Config7`
- Model / role: `Worklist-PC-5` / `worklist-workstation`
- Deployment group: `worklist`
- OS: `Windows 11 IoT Enterprise` build `10.0.22621.2500`
- Clinical criticality: `low`
- Network exposure: `enterprise_lan`

## Vendor vs product scores

| | Severity | Likelihood | Risk |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Vendor | `C` | `C` | `C` |
| Product | `L` | `L` | `L` |

## Technical Impact Assessment

### Impacted Components

`HostApplication.csproj` `OutputType=WinExe` and `app.manifest` `assemblyIdentity` define how Windows launches the product executable.

### Potential Risks

- **Required for the app to keep working: Not required.** Executable identity is declared in `app.manifest`; Shell components are not PackageReferences.
- **If we install: App may break.** Shell cumulative updates can change Explorer presentation of WinExe identities until reboot.
- **If we skip: No effect on the app.** FindUpdates BLOCK/HOLD: skipping does not block Host Application startup; bundled runtime is unchanged.
- **Compatibility: Compatible with the app.** WinExe on `main` already starts on this image; policy keeps the row at Low Prio.

### Conclusions

Shell KB does not alter bits inside the published self-contained executable.

## Cybersecurity impact assessment

This patch fixes CVE-2026-32202 in Windows Shell. SBOM scan and source code scan revealed there is no such dependency in our code. No shell32 usage in `MainViewModel` or Core libraries on `main`.

## Product Risk assessment

- **Functions affected:** Launch via WinExe/manifest only; notes, sysinfo, and bulletin paths unchanged if KB is skipped.
- **Hazards:** None identified for this product configuration when the update is not installed.
- **Install vs skip:** Install still carries shell servicing risk; skip aligns with FindUpdates BLOCK and does not stop the app.

## Test Planning

### Recommended Regression Suite

- None. No documented test covers this coupling.

### Gap Analysis

- None. No documented test covers shell-launch coupling.

## Recommendation

Maintain FindUpdates BLOCK on this configuration: record Low Prio evidence only; do not treat as product patch authorization.

findings.title: Vendor bulletin HTTPS accepts any server certificate
findings.evidence: src/HostApplication.Core/InsecureVendorBulletinClient.cs: AcceptAnyServerCertificate returns sslPolicyErrors == SslPolicyErrors.None (not unconditional trust); Marker TLS_CERTIFICATE_VALIDATED; tests/HostApplication.Tests/InsecureVendorBulletinClientTests.cs TC-REG-TLS-CALLBACK rejects invalid chains. No INTENTIONAL_SKILL_TEST_VULNERABILITY in the TLS client. inputs/vulnerability-report.md and docs/mds2.md MDS2-TLS row describe the pre-patch bypass and are stale relative to main code.

findings.title: Notes stored as plaintext in user AppData
findings.evidence: src/HostApplication.Core/NoteStore.cs writes UTF-8 plaintext under ApplicationData\HostApplication\notes.txt with no network export; MDS2-DATA (inputs/mds2.md) met — local notes only, no PHI.

findings.title: No inbound network listener
findings.evidence: No TcpListener/HttpListener/Kestrel or bind usage in workspace/HostApplication source; MDS2-NET (inputs/mds2.md) met — optional outbound HTTPS GET only.
